1	Run only the Conditional Access tests with Invoke-Maester -Tag CA.
     2	Run one test with Invoke-Maester -TestId MT.1001. Wildcards work too: -TestId 'CISA.MS.AAD.*'.
     3	See what would run, and why other tests would not, with Invoke-Maester -DryRun.
     4	Connect more services with Connect-Maester -Service All, or name them: -Service Graph, Teams.
     5	Set severities, turn tests off and pass parameters to tests in maester-config.json.
     6	Add -IncludeAffectedObjects to list the users, groups and apps each finding refers to.
     7	Add -IncludePreview and -IncludeLongRunning to run the tests that are left out by default.
     8	Choose the panels of this dashboard with Output.DashboardPanels in maester-config.json.
     9	Get-MtTest lists every test with its product, severity and tags, without connecting to a tenant.
    10	Write your own test with New-MtTest -Id CONTOSO.1001 -Title '...'.
    11	Send the results by mail or to Teams with -MailRecipient or -TeamChannelWebhookUri.
    12	Use -OutputMode Plain for output without colour or symbols, and -OutputMode Stream for lines only.
    13	Run Maester on a schedule in GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps: see maester.dev/docs/monitoring.
    14	Create the app for unattended runs, with its permissions granted, in one line: New-MtMaesterApp.

function Get-MtTest {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Lists Maester native tests and their metadata without connecting to a tenant.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Without -Path, returns the tests that ship with Maester (the catalog). With -Path, reads the native
    tests (Test.<ID>.ps1) in a file or folder and validates them; each object's Errors property lists
    every problem with its line, and IsValid is $false when there is one. No test code is run.

    .PARAMETER Id
    Only tests with these IDs: exact IDs or '*' wildcards.

    .PARAMETER Tag
    Only tests that any of these tags select: a tag the test carries or, for a test that ships with Maester,
    its ID or one of the tags it carried in Maester 2.x.

    .PARAMETER Product
    Only tests of these products: keys such as entra, or an alias such as 'Entra ID'. Matches a test's
    Product or any of its RelatedProduct values. '*' wildcards are allowed.

    .PARAMETER Feature
    Only tests about these features of a product, for example conditional-access.

    .PARAMETER Area
    Only tests of these security areas, for example authentication.

    .PARAMETER Severity
    Only tests with these severities: Critical, High, Medium, Low or Info.

    .PARAMETER Suite
    Only tests of these suites, for example Maester, CISA or AD.

    .PARAMETER Path
    A Test.<ID>.ps1 file or a folder of them to validate.

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtTest -Product entra -Severity High | Format-Table Id, Title, Feature, Area

    Lists the built-in Entra ID tests of high severity. The values of one selector are alternatives; different
    selectors must all match.

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtTest -Path ./Custom | Where-Object { -not $_.IsValid } | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Errors

    Shows every problem in the custom tests.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Get-MtTest
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Position = 0)]
        [string[]] $Id,

<!-- Generated by build/github/Update-AgentFiles.ps1 from .github/agents and .github/skills. Edit those files, then run the script. -->

# Agents and skills

The Maester repository ships AI agents and skills that know its conventions: how a check is written,
which attributes it needs, how pull requests and issues are labelled. They work in
[GitHub Copilot](https://docs.github.com/copilot) and [Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code)
when you open the repository. [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/AGENTS.md) holds the rules every agent follows.

## Agents

An agent is a role with its own instructions and tools. Ask for it by name, for example
"use maester-test-planner to plan a check for guest invite settings".

| Agent | For | What it does | How to use it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`maester-issue-manager`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/.github/agents/maester-issue-manager.agent.md) | Contributors and maintainers | Reserves MT test IDs on issue #697 and keeps tracking issues tidy for new checks. | Called by the other agents, or ask Claude Code to use it |
| [`maester-test-expert`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/.github/agents/maester-test-expert.agent.md) | Contributors writing or reviewing checks | Writes, reviews and documents checks, including their attributes and the Test.<ID>.md guide. | Pick it in Copilot's agent list, or ask Claude Code to use it |
| [`maester-test-planner`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/.github/agents/maester-test-planner.agent.md) | Contributors planning a new check | Plans a new or changed check before any code is written: files, attributes, validation steps. | Called by the other agents, or ask Claude Code to use it |
| [`maester-triage`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/.github/agents/maester-triage.agent.md) | Maintainers and reviewers | Labels and re-labels PRs, issues and discussions with the label rubric so the queue can be filtered. | Pick it in Copilot's agent list, or ask Claude Code to use it |

## Skills

A skill is a body of knowledge an agent loads when the task needs it. The agents above read these, and
any agent can follow them directly.

| Skill | For | What it covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`maester-test-expert`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/.github/skills/maester-test-expert/SKILL.md) | Contributors writing or reviewing checks | The full guide to writing a check: layout, templates, attributes, rubric, validation and remediation. |

## Changing an agent or skill

Each agent and skill has one source file, which GitHub Copilot reads:

- an agent is `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md`
- a skill is `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`

Everything else is generated from those files by `build/github/Update-AgentFiles.ps1`: the Claude Code copies under
`.claude/agents/` and `.claude/skills/`, and this page. Never edit the generated files.

To add or change one:

1. Edit or create the source file. Its frontmatter needs `name` and `description`, and a
   `metadata` block with `audience` (who uses it) and `summary` (one sentence on what it does).
   An agent also needs `metadata.claude-tools`: the Claude Code tools it may use, or `all`.
2. Run `./build/github/Update-AgentFiles.ps1`.
3. Commit the source file and the generated files together. `powershell/tests/general/AgentFiles.Tests.ps1`
   fails the build when a generated file is out of date.

Each folder here is a [Maester Pack](https://maester.dev/docs/packs) that is part of the Maester module:
a `maester-pack.json`, its suites of native tests, and its helpers and connectors.

﻿function Get-MtArgumentCompleterTable {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Lists the parameters whose values Maester completes with Tab: Command, Parameter, Kind, Values and Narrow.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Register-MtArgumentCompleter registers one completer for each row, and Get-MtArgumentCompletion looks the row
    up to know what to list. Kind names the values (Get-MtCompletionCandidate). Values are a command's own names
    for the Service kind. Narrow is false for a selector whose list does not depend on the other selectors on the
    line: -ExcludeProduct may leave out any product.

    Every Command must be an exported command with the Parameter; the unit tests check each row.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param()

    $row = {
        param([string] $Command, [string] $Parameter, [string] $Kind, [string[]] $Values = @(), [bool] $Narrow = $true)
        [pscustomobject]@{ Command = $Command; Parameter = $Parameter; Kind = $Kind; Values = $Values; Narrow = $Narrow }
    }

    # The selectors of a run, and Get-MtTest, which selects the same way.
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Product' 'Product'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'ExcludeProduct' 'Product' -Narrow $false
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Feature' 'Feature'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Area' 'Area'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Severity' 'Severity'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Suite' 'Suite'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Tag' 'Tag'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'ExcludeTag' 'Tag'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'TestId' 'TestId'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'ExcludeTestId' 'TestId'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Pack' 'Pack'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Id' 'TestId'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Tag' 'Tag'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Product' 'Product'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Feature' 'Feature'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Area' 'Area'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Severity' 'Severity'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Suite' 'Suite'
    & $row 'Invoke-MtTest' 'Id' 'TestId'

    # Writing a test: the keys the taxonomy allows, whatever tests exist.
    & $row 'New-MtTest' 'Product' 'TaxonomyProduct'
    & $row 'New-MtTest' 'Feature' 'TaxonomyFeature'
    & $row 'New-MtTest' 'Area' 'TaxonomyArea'
    & $row 'New-MtTest' 'ResourceType' 'ResourceType'
    & $row 'New-MtTest' 'Mitre' 'Mitre'
    & $row 'New-MtTest' 'Service' 'TestService'

    # Packs: Invoke-Maester -Pack takes a code or an ID; the pack commands take IDs.
    & $row 'Get-MtPack' 'Id' 'PackId'
    & $row 'Restore-MtPack' 'Id' 'InstalledPackId'
    & $row 'Update-MtPack' 'Id' 'InstalledPackId'
    & $row 'Uninstall-MtPack' 'Id' 'InstalledPackId'

    # Connections: each command's own service names (as its Resolve-MtRequestedService call has them), then the

    & $row 'Connect-Maester' 'Service' 'Service' @('ActiveDirectory', 'All', 'Azure', 'Dataverse', 'ExchangeOnline', 'GitHub', 'Graph', 'SecurityCompliance', 'Teams', 'SharePointOnline')
    & $row 'Test-MtConnection' 'Service' 'Service' @('ActiveDirectory', 'All', 'Azure', 'AzureDevOps', 'ExchangeOnline', 'EOP', 'GitHub', 'Graph', 'SecurityCompliance', 'SharePointOnline', 'Teams')
    & $row 'Get-MtConnector' 'Service' 'Service'

    & $row 'Get-MtSetting' 'Name' 'Setting'
    & $row 'Get-MtRoleMember' 'Role' 'Role'
}
